name: Voltage sensor module (0-25 V, 5:1 divider)
description: Passive DC voltage sensor: a 30 kΩ / 7.5 kΩ resistive divider that scales the voltage on its screw terminal down by 5 (V(S) = Vin / 5), so an ADC can read up to 25 V with a 5 V reference (about 16 V on a 3.3 V board). No chip and no supply pin. Sold as: blue "Voltage Sensor Module DC 0-25V" (generic clone), screw terminal VCC/GND for the measured source and 3-pin header S, +, - (+ not connected).
eli5: Two resistors that shrink a big voltage, like a 12 V battery, to one fifth so your board can measure it safely.

pins.name: S
pins.description: Analog output, Vin / 5 (header pin 1). Wire to an ADC pin.
Not connected on the board (header pin 2).
Ground (header pin 3): MCU GND, same net as the screw terminal GND.

buildNotes: Header order: S, +, -. The + pin is not connected; - is ground and must go to the MCU GND.
Measured source goes to the screw terminal: + to VCC, - to GND. DC only, observe polarity.
On a 3.3 V board keep Vin below about 15 V (ESP32) / 16.5 V (Pico), or S exceeds the ADC range and can damage the pin.
The measured source's negative is tied to the MCU ground through the module.

example.code:
from voltsense import VoltageSensor
import time

vs = VoltageSensor({S})
while True:
    print('V=%.1f' % vs.volts())
    time.sleep(0.5)

test.title: Reports the voltage on the screw terminal

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading. Not yet tested on real hardware.
